previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of paraplegia from a gunshot wound, chronic indwelling Foley catheter, and neurogenic bladder presented with suprapubic and right flank pain, nausea, poor appetite, and foul-smelling urine for three days. She was admitted for possible urinary tract infection and treated with IV ceftriaxone and levofloxacin, later transitioning to oral cefpodoxime. A femoral line was placed for access and removed prior to discharge. Urine culture showed yeast, and she received fluconazole for candidiasis. The Foley catheter was exchanged during admission, and urology follow-up was arranged to discuss suprapubic catheter placement. Renal ultrasound showed no abscess or stones. She also reported bilateral hand and foot swelling, which will be evaluated by a newly arranged primary care provider. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor a skin tear on her right inner thigh and return if symptoms worsened.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Urinary catheterization as the cause of abnormal reaction of patient, or of later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of procedure
Late effect of spinal cord injury
Late effects of injury, undetermined whether accidentally or purposely inflicted
